result.summary: Verdict FINDINGS at exact target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (feature/binary-config-serve-20260930). Scope: pause/resume ordering, timeout suspension, retries, pending intents under concurrency. 2 findings, both reproduced with the repo's own fakes. (1) MEDIUM coordinator.ts:440 - a control intent recorded while a step is in flight survives that step's terminal transition (store.finish store.ts:291 and fail coordinator.ts:800-804 leave w.intent set; runTick :345 admits any worker with an intent), so the next tick applies it via applyControl and regresses completed->paused and recovery_required->paused, holding capacity and stranding an accepted send_worker_message (delivery:queued, dispatch stays pending until an unrequested resume). (2) LOW coordinator.ts:235 - queueMessage stamps provision_started_at while paused and resume adds the whole pause elapsed (:863), so the 300s boot guard became ~3900s after a 1h pause. No source changes; targeted suites 58 pass/0 fail.
result.details:
Method: fetched the target branch, cloned a disposable detached checkout at /tmp/rev-scope/checkout, verified git rev-parse HEAD = d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895. /workspace/repo left at baseline 5672ead2a526e07fea9ed11e58b3725e42013527, clean, untouched. Bun 1.4.2 installed to /tmp/rev-scope/bun142 (snapshot Bun 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2); bun install --frozen-lockfile exit 0, lockfile not rewritten.

F1 MEDIUM (reproduced): runControl stores the intent then awaits exclusive(), which returns the already-running step, so control never runs its own step. When that step settles the worker (finish -> completed, ambiguous-delivery recovery_required at :573, or fail -> failed/recovery_required) the intent is left set. The next tick's filter (w.intent || ...) includes terminal workers, and applyControl's pause branch has no terminal guard, so the state regresses. Reproduced with gated agent.inspect: completed->paused (previous_state completed, events worker.completed -> worker.paused) and recovery_required->paused. Impact: masks a state the docs require the operator to act on, holds a MAX_WORKERS slot, and a follow-up message is acknowledged with delivery:queued yet never delivered (step is only reached for non-paused states). Why guards miss it: lifecycle.test.ts:309-336 and :562-598 cover destroy-during-reconcile and cancel-behind-an-in-flight-step; fail's missing-VM branch clears intent on purpose, but no test lets an intent wait behind monitor()/complete(), and lifecycle.test.ts:286-298 makes pause-on-completed look intentional. Fix: drop/refuse intents that lost a race to a terminal transition (only cancel/destroy may act on terminal states) and clear intent in store.finish and fail's settled transitions.

F2 LOW (reproduced): queueMessage resets provision_started_at to now while paused; resume then adds the entire pause elapsed, double counting the pre-message part, so the boot guard at :444-451 cannot fire for that long. Measured 3900s window instead of 300s after a 1h pause. Fix: keep the original stamp or clamp the shift to time since the stamp.

Checked and sound: deadline/provision/token-idle clocks are suspended while paused and shifted once on resume; send_worker_message linearization via tearingDown plus cancel/destroy intent (the enqueue at :225 and the throw at :232 share one db.transaction, verified no dispatch leak); spawn request_id retry fingerprint over normalized input; resume/cancel retry keeps VM and intent; worker.resumed cannot surface as a state via lifecycleState().

No secrets, canaries or credential-shaped examples were captured in the artifacts; the Redactor-sensitive paths were not exercised with real values.

Full suite not run (whole-suite reviewer); probes exit 0.
